pol-cmp-01-c1.text: Guillermo O'Donnell (2000). Democracy, Law, and Comparative Politics. Kellogg Institute for International Studies, University of Notre Dame, Working Paper #274.
pol-cmp-01-c1.quote: This is the paradigmatic 'minimalist' (or 'processualist') definition of democracy.
pol-cmp-01-c1.claim: offered a deliberately minimalist procedural definition. For him, democracy is the institutional arrangement in which individuals acquire the power to decide by means of a competitive struggle for the people's vote

pol-cmp-07-c1.text: Massachusetts Historical Society. The Gerry-Mander. A new species of Monster which appeared in Essex South District in Jan. 1812 [broadside, Salem, 1812]. MHS Collections Online.
pol-cmp-07-c1.quote: the Massachusetts law that gave rise to the name dates from 11 February 1812, when Governor Elbridge Gerry, a Jeffersonian Republican, signed a reapportioning act that heavily favored his own party
pol-cmp-07-c1.claim: governor Elbridge Gerry signed the redistricting act on 11 February 1812

pol-cmp-07-c1.text: Dimunation, M. (2024). Gerrymandering: The Origin Story. Library of Congress, Timeless blog.
pol-cmp-07-c1.quote: The newly drawn state senate district in Essex County was lampooned in cartoons as a strange winged dragon, clutching at the region.
pol-cmp-07-c1.claim: the contorted 1812 district was a Massachusetts state senate district in Essex County, drawn in cartoons as a winged monster

pol-cmp-07-c1.text: Allen, E. (2012). Terminology in Office. Library of Congress Blog.
pol-cmp-07-c1.quote: A political cartoon-map delineating these redrawn electoral districts first appeared in the Boston Gazette for March 26, 1812.
pol-cmp-07-c1.claim: the Boston Gazette printed the Gerry-mander cartoon on 26 March 1812

pol-cmp-07-c1.text: Li, M. (2021, updated 2026). Gerrymandering Explained. Brennan Center for Justice.
pol-cmp-07-c1.quote: With packing, map drawers cram members of disfavored groups or parties into as few districts as possible.
pol-cmp-07-c1.claim: packing concentrates the other side's voters in a few districts they win overwhelmingly

pol-cmp-07-c1.text: Li, M. (2021, updated 2026). Gerrymandering Explained. Brennan Center for Justice.
pol-cmp-07-c1.quote: Cracking splits groups of disfavored voters among multiple districts.
pol-cmp-07-c1.claim: cracking spreads the other side's voters across many districts so they are too few to win in any

pol-cmp-07-c1.text: Stephanopoulos, N. O. & McGhee, E. M. (2015). Partisan Gerrymandering and the Efficiency Gap. University of Chicago Law Review 82(2): 831–900.
pol-cmp-07-c1.quote: Wasted votes include both “lost” votes (those cast for a losing candidate) and “surplus” votes (those cast for a winning candidate but in excess of what she needed to prevail).
pol-cmp-07-c1.claim: wasted votes are votes for losing candidates plus winners' votes beyond what they needed

pol-cmp-07-c2.text: Stephanopoulos, N. O. & McGhee, E. M. (2015). Partisan Gerrymandering and the Efficiency Gap. University of Chicago Law Review 82(2): 831–900.
pol-cmp-07-c2.quote: It represents the difference between the parties’ respective wasted votes in an election, divided by the total number of votes cast.
pol-cmp-07-c2.claim: the efficiency gap is the difference between the two parties' wasted votes divided by all votes cast

pol-cmp-07-c2.text: Stephanopoulos, N. O. & McGhee, E. M. (2015). Partisan Gerrymandering and the Efficiency Gap. University of Chicago Law Review 82(2): 831–900.
pol-cmp-07-c2.quote: We propose setting thresholds above which plans would be presumptively unconstitutional: two seats for congressional plans and 8 percent for state house plans, but only if the plans probably will stay unbalanced for the remainder of the cycle.
pol-cmp-07-c2.claim: the authors proposed presumptive-unconstitutionality thresholds of two seats for congressional plans and 8 percent for state house plans

pol-cmp-07-c2.text: Chen, J. & Rodden, J. (2013). Unintentional Gerrymandering: Political Geography and Electoral Bias in Legislatures. Quarterly Journal of Political Science 8(3): 239–269.
pol-cmp-07-c2.quote: We show that in many states, Democrats are inefficiently concentrated in large cities and smaller industrial agglomerations such that they can expect to win fewer than 50% of the seats when they win 50% of the votes.
pol-cmp-07-c2.claim: democrats' concentration in cities produces pro-Republican bias in district maps even without intentional gerrymandering

pol-cmp-07-c2.text: League of Women Voters of Pennsylvania v. Commonwealth, 178 A.3d 737 (Pa. 2018) (Todd, J., majority opinion, Feb. 7, 2018). Supreme Court of Pennsylvania.
pol-cmp-07-c2.quote: In order to evaluate the 2011 plan, Dr. Chen testified that he used a computer algorithm to create two sets, each with 500 plans, of computer-simulated redistricting plans for Pennsylvania’s congressional districts.
pol-cmp-07-c2.claim: expert Jowei Chen compared Pennsylvania's 2011 congressional map with 1,000 computer-simulated alternative maps

pol-cmp-07-c2.text: League of Women Voters of Pennsylvania v. Commonwealth, 178 A.3d 737 (Pa. 2018) (Todd, J., majority opinion, Feb. 7, 2018). Supreme Court of Pennsylvania.
pol-cmp-07-c2.quote: He further testified the 2011 Plan “was indeed an extreme outlier with respect to partisan bias in a way that could not be explained by the interaction of political geography and the districting criteria” that he considered.
pol-cmp-07-c2.claim: expert Wesley Pegden's random-map analysis showed the 2011 map was an extreme partisan outlier; the court struck the map down under the state constitution

pol-cmp-07-c3.text: Wesberry v. Sanders, 376 U.S. 1 (1964) (Black, J., opinion of the Court, decided Feb. 17, 1964). Supreme Court of the United States.
pol-cmp-07-c3.quote: as nearly as is practicable one man's vote in a congressional election is to be worth as much as another's.
pol-cmp-07-c3.claim: the equal-population rule applies to US House districts

pol-cmp-07-c3.text: Reynolds v. Sims, 377 U.S. 533 (1964) (Warren, C.J., opinion of the Court, decided June 15, 1964). Supreme Court of the United States.
pol-cmp-07-c3.quote: Legislators represent people, not trees or acres.
pol-cmp-07-c3.claim: state legislators represent people, not land, so districts must be based on population

pol-cmp-07-c3.text: Rucho v. Common Cause, 588 U.S. 684 (2019) (Roberts, C.J., opinion of the Court, 5–4, decided June 27, 2019). Supreme Court of the United States.
pol-cmp-07-c3.quote: We conclude that partisan gerrymandering claims present political questions beyond the reach of the federal courts.
pol-cmp-07-c3.claim: in a 5–4 opinion by Chief Justice Roberts, the Court held partisan gerrymandering claims are political questions federal courts cannot decide

pol-cmp-07-c3.text: Allen v. Milligan, 599 U.S. 1 (2023) (Roberts, C.J., opinion of the Court, 5–4, decided June 8, 2023). Supreme Court of the United States.
pol-cmp-07-c3.quote: The Court faithfully applied our precedents and correctly determined that, under existing law, HB1 violated §2.
pol-cmp-07-c3.claim: allen v. Milligan (2023) upheld the finding that Alabama's congressional map likely violated Section 2

pol-cmp-07-c3.text: Louisiana v. Callais, 608 U.S. ___ (2026), Nos. 24–109 and 24–110 (Alito, J., opinion of the Court, 6–3, decided April 29, 2026). Supreme Court of the United States.
pol-cmp-07-c3.quote: In short, §2 imposes liability only when the evidence supports a strong inference that the State intentionally drew its districts to afford minority voters less opportunity because of their race.
pol-cmp-07-c3.claim: callais narrowed Section 2 to cases with a strong inference of intentional discrimination

pol-cmp-07-c3.text: Arizona State Legislature v. Arizona Independent Redistricting Commission, 576 U.S. 787 (2015) (Ginsburg, J., opinion of the Court, 5–4, decided June 29, 2015). Supreme Court of the United States.
pol-cmp-07-c3.quote: The Elections Clause permits the people of Arizona to provide for redistricting by independent commission.
pol-cmp-07-c3.claim: the Supreme Court upheld voters' power to hand congressional redistricting to an independent commission

pol-cmp-07-c3.text: California Citizens Redistricting Commission. About Us. WeDrawTheLines.ca.gov.
pol-cmp-07-c3.quote: California voters authorized the creation of the Commission when they passed the VOTERS FIRST Act (Act) in 2008.
pol-cmp-07-c3.claim: voters created the commission in 2008 (Voters FIRST Act) and added congressional districts in 2010

pol-cmp-07-c3.claim: california's Citizens Redistricting Commission was created by Proposition 11 (2008) and given congressional maps by Proposition 20 (2010)

pol-cmp-07-c3.claim: the commissions work independently of ministers

pol-cmp-07-c3.claim: in Londonderry about 60% of adults were Catholic yet Unionists held 60% of Corporation seats (1967: 14,429 Catholic vs 8,781 other voters; 12 Unionist vs 8 non-Unionist councillors)
